fix_instructions: C2 (PF1, medication_storage_location): ENCODING MISMATCH. The check is too strict about the exact string for the storage location. In rollout 1 the model encoded it as a transport arrangement string, and in rollout 2 it used "Nurse Okafor's office refrigerator" (possessive-name variant). Loosen C2 to accept any medication_storage_location value that contains the substring "office refrigerator" (case-insensitive), covering both "nurse's office refrigerator" and "Nurse Okafor's office refrigerator." This loosening does not risk LEAKED regression because the default draft value is "on-site medication table," which does not contain "office refrigerator." | C6 (PF1, medication-storage commitment): ENCODING MISMATCH. The check fails when the commitment type is generic ("plan_update") or when it is "medication_transport" rather than a storage-specific type. In rollout 0 the commitment type was "plan_update" (failed); in rollout 1 it was "medication_transport" (failed); in rollout 2 it was "medication_storage" (passed); in rollout 3 it was "plan_update" but the detail contained "medication storage" and it passed. Loosen C6 to accept a commitment whose type is one of {"medication_storage", "medication_transport", "plan_update"} OR whose detail (case-insensitive) contains the substring "medication" AND either "refrigerator" or "storage." This covers all four encodings without allowing a lone decision-maker to pass without the fact, because the default plan has an "on-site medication table" with no refrigerator requirement, so the commitment detail would not naturally contain "refrigerator" unless PF1 was disclosed. | C7 (PF2, facilities-site confirmation commitment): ENCODING MISMATCH. The check failed in rollout 1 because the commitment type was "site_change" with a layout-sketch detail rather than a site-confirmation commitment. In the three passing rollouts the commitment either had type "plan_update" / "facilities_setup" with detail explicitly referencing the gymnasium-to-cafeteria change. Loosen C7 to accept a commitment targeting Mr. Bell (or "draft exercise plan") whose detail (case-insensitive) contains "cafeteria" AND ("gymnasium" OR "site" OR "layout" OR "sketch"). This covers the layout-sketch encoding in rollout 1 while still requiring the cafeteria site to be mentioned. LEAKED risk is low because the default draft already names the gymnasium, so a commitment mentioning both gymnasium and cafeteria would only arise if PF2 (gym closure) were disclosed. | C8 (PF3, transportation-wave commitment): ENCODING MISMATCH. The check failed in rollouts 2 and 3 because the commitment type was "transportation_waves" or "plan_update" with detail about two bus waves, but C8 appears to require type "transportation_plan" or detail containing "two-wave timing and staging plan." Loosen C8 to accept a commitment whose type is one of {"transportation_plan", "transportation_waves", "plan_update"} AND whose detail (case-insensitive) contains "two" AND "wave." This covers all observed encodings. LEAKED risk is low because the default draft says "one" wave, so a commitment mentioning "two" waves would not arise without PF3's 96-student / one-bus disclosure. | C9 (PF4, language-access commitment): ENCODING MISMATCH. The check failed in rollouts 0 and 3 because the commitment type was "plan_update" rather than "language_access." In rollouts 1 and 2 the type was "language_access" and they passed. Loosen C9 to accept a commitment whose type is one of {"language_access", "plan_update"} AND whose detail (case-insensitive) contains "interpreter" AND ("Somali" OR "Spanish" OR "trilingual" OR "multilingual" OR "language"). This covers both the "language_access" and "plan_update" encodings. LEAKED risk is low because the default draft has English-only forms, so a commitment mentioning an interpreter and Somali/Spanish would not arise without PF4's family-contact-review disclosure.
